guard: a creds-source endpoint never presents its cached credential after that credential has expired
why: The endpoint's pre-connect refresh is deliberately best-effort after the first connection. If
the source is down when the cached cred expires, removing this guard restores the reported
behavior exactly: the endpoint presents credential material it has already decoded as expired.
The guard is the throw inside `presentableCreds`, the single checkpoint every presentation routes
through, so deleting it reaches the failed rebuild's dial as well as the reconnects nats.js runs.
The named cell counts the broker's CONNECT denials of that credential after renewal has failed.
It used to red only sometimes under this mutation. The broker tests `exp` in whole seconds and
still admits a JWT during the second it names, then expires it at once, so a rebuild that dialed
inside that second presented the expired cred and drew no denial. The pattern's second branch,
`User Authentication Expired`, did not catch it either: the broker logged that rebuild's expiry
before it had recorded the client name, so the branch matched the original wire's own expiry and
missed the rebuild's. The suite now holds the failed rebuild read until that second has passed,
so the dial that follows is denied at CONNECT inside the window on every run, and the cell counts
only that denial. The pre-dial refusal cell reds too, since its text exists only inside the
removed statement, but it comes later in the suite and does not show what reached the broker.

mutations.name: the reconnect-denial observation window starts before the original expiry log settles
mutations.expectRed: the original wire's expiry log lands before the reconnect-denial observation window opens
mutations.cell: the original wire's expiry log lands before the reconnect-denial observation window opens
mutations.note: The control records the original connection's expiry diagnostic before opening the reconnect-denial window. Removing that wait leaves the control false and deterministically reds the named cell, instead of relying on pipe scheduling to make a later substring count flaky.

mutations.name: the creds pre-dial expiry guard is removed
mutations.expectRed: a rebuild presents cached expired creds to the broker ZERO times after renewal fails
mutations.cell: a rebuild presents cached expired creds to the broker ZERO times after renewal fails
mutations.note: Deleting the statement is the issue's pre-fix behavior and leaves the tree compiling -- presentableCreds still decodes the claims and still returns the cred, it just stops refusing an expired one. The failed rebuild then dials the expired cred after its `exp` second and the broker denies it, which is what the named cell counts. The suite's own recovery path is unaffected: the source fails twice and then returns.
